subject: QBR pre-read: runway sizing & unit-econ sensitivity (micro-batching + KV-cache)
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-01T16:08:00Z
Subject: QBR pre-read: runway sizing & unit-econ sensitivity (micro-batching + KV-cache)

Team —

Ahead of the QBR next week I pulled together a compact pre-read focused on runway sizing and the unit economics levers we can pull in the short term. Key items are:

- Current committed GPU spend and runway at projected growth rates (sheet tab A).
- Observed GPU utilization by model family and slot type (tab B).
- Micro-batching and prefix/KV-cache sensitivity: representative % cost savings at 95th/50th latency SLOs (tab C).
- Two downside scenarios: demand surge (+35% token volume) and price shock (+15% GPU hourly).

Please review the attached "runway-sensitivity-v2.xlsx" and the short summary PDF. I want the leadership check-in to surface the single ask/decision point for each site:

1) How much guaranteed dedicated capacity do we want to recommend for the customer-facing hosted tier vs. dedicated pools?
2) Which micro-batching experiments should we accelerate into production before QBR to validate the mid/high-latency tradeoffs?
3) Do we accept a conservative KV-cache policy (longer TTL, slightly higher memory) to preserve unit cost, or prioritize lower memory usage to reduce infra footprint?

Specific asks for you:
- Markus: can you sanity-check the cost model inputs on tab A (spot vs reserved breakouts) and call out any hidden line items?
- Karthik: please confirm the utilization samples in tab B; I know you have cluster-level traces that might change the averages.
- Olga: any compliance or procurement constraints that should temper a recommendation on guaranteed capacity?

I'm aiming to lock the deck by EOD Monday (2026-05-04) so we can circulate to Exec on Tuesday. If we can get a prioritized list of 1) must-have experiments and 2) optional mitigations, we can include clear decision asks in the QBR.

Thanks —

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Infrastructure & Platform
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: runway-sensitivity-v2.xlsx, microbatch-experiments-summary.pdf, kvcache-hitrate-snapshots.png
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-02T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR pre-read: runway sizing & unit-econ sensitivity (micro-batching + KV-cache)

Thanks Lauren — quick read done. A couple of notes inline and attached a small pivot of the cost tabs.

- Tab A (cost inputs): I flagged three items that materially shift run rate:
  * Reserved instance amortization: current model amortizes at 36 months; if we move to a 12-month commit for Dedicated we need to adjust monthly SLR.
  * Inter-region egress: we've been under-counting cross-region traffic for embeddings-heavy workloads (impact ~3% of infra spend).
  * Support overhead: I added an explicit 5% ops staffing markup — we should decide whether it remains in product opex or infra budget.

- Tab B (utilization): the cluster traces I ran show our 95th percentile GPU slot utilization is ~12% lower than the sample in the sheet during the 18:00–22:00 window; this is likely because smaller request-size models incur lower KV-cache reuse. If true, that widens the headroom for batching before we hit tail-latency issues.

- Micro-batching experiments: I agree we should accelerate two pilots before QBR: 1) adaptive batch sizing (per-slot with latency guardrails), 2) prefix-prefetching to improve KV cache hit-rate. The PDF summarizes the expected TCO improvement (est. 9–14% cost per 1M tokens for adaptive batching + 6–9% for prefix-prefetching depending on model mix).

I attached "runway-sensitivity-markus-pivots.xlsx" with redline comments. My recommendation: present two runway options to Exec — conservative (no change to reserved commitments, prioritize KV) and aggressive (10% reserved reduction + batch rollout). We should show the NPV over 12 months.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: runway-sensitivity-markus-pivots.xlsx
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-03T14:50:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR pre-read: runway sizing & unit-econ sensitivity (micro-batching + KV-cache)

Adding the utilization traces and a short note on measurement methodology.

Key clarifications:
- The earlier sample used for tab B averaged per-request GPU occupancy across model families; that biases upward for larger-context models. My trace extract (attached) segments utilization by model and by sequence length percentile — that produced the lower 95th for smaller models Markus noted.
- KV-cache hit-rate: the snapshot (attached PNG) shows current hit-rate ~24% for conversational models in production; enabling prefix-prefetching for the same cohort pushes that to ~46% on our test harness. The cost reduction from improved hit-rate is nonlinear because it reduces both token generation and repeat KV lookups.
- Micro-batching impact on latency: our sim shows adaptive batching (with a 20ms service-level latency guard) preserves 95th latency for low-priority routes while improving cost ~10% for those routes. Heavy tail routes (multi-tool calls) still need stricter per-request handling.

Ask: I've provided a 2-slide appendix (in Drive link) summarizing the methodology and the raw traces. If you want, I can convert the traces into a single-page graph for the QBR deck.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: k8s-utilization-traces-0503.csv, kvcache-hitrate-snapshots.png
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-04T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR pre-read: runway sizing & unit-econ sensitivity (micro-batching + KV-cache)

Acknowledged — thank you for the quick turn. A few procurement/op constraints to flag for Exec:

- Procurement lead time: moving to a shorter reserved term (12 months) improves cash flow but requires faster reprocurement and reduces negotiating leverage; ops should be prepared for a 6–9 week timeline for SKU changes.
- Compliance: for some regulated customers we must guarantee slot isolation; this limits how aggressive we can be with cross-tenant micro-batching. We'll surface a one-pager showing which customer cohorts require isolated pools.
- Marketplace commitments: Aurora Labs program requires a minimum committed baseline for a co-sell promotion; if we reduce reserved capacity too far we risk losing a portion of the Marketplace incentive.

I'll prepare a short slide with the procurement timeline and the list of customers impacted by isolation requirements. Recommend we present three ask-lines in the QBR:
1) Approve a 6-week pilot window for adaptive batching on non-isolated tenant pools.
2) Approve a conservative change to reserved terms (hybrid 18-month) with an exec review at 6 weeks.
3) Approve prioritization of KV-cache prefetching experiments to reach a 40%+ hit-rate for conversational models.

- Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Global Procurement & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: procurement-timeline-onepager.pdf
